title: Sacred houses may not be dedicated to angels or Saints for cult, though ancient memorials of martyrs are not condemned
source_text: XXV. Itaque prorsus illicitum putant Angelis, & hominibus Sanctis in caelum receptis, aedes sacras dicare, non tantum ut illis ibi sacrificium offeratur, sed etiam ut illic ritibus quibuscunque colantur atque invocentur, quanquam non damnent morem Ecclesiae veteris, in qua solenne fuit aedes sacras inter alia eo fine struere ut ibi memoria Martyrum conservaretur, & gratiae Deo agerentur de victoriis per Dei gratiam ab iis reportatis, eoque nomine sacrificia Eucharistica Deo offerrentur, quod in Sanctorum virorum maximum honorem cedebat. Ut apud Andream Rivetum videre est, in consideratione ad articulum tertium Judicii viri docti, de ejus Apologia pro Beata Virgine, quod in fine illius Apologiae legitur.
pass_a_gloss: And so they think it altogether unlawful to dedicate sacred buildings to angels and to holy men received into heaven, not only so that sacrifice may be offered to them there, but also so that they may be cultivated and invoked there with any rites whatever, although they do not condemn the custom of the ancient Church, in which it was solemn to build sacred buildings, among other things, for this end, that the memory of the Martyrs might be preserved there, and thanks given to God for the victories obtained by them through the grace of God, and in that name Eucharistic sacrifices offered to God, which redounded to the greatest honor of holy men. As may be seen in Andrew Rivet, in the consideration on the third article of the Judgment of a learned man, concerning his Apology for the Blessed Virgin, which is read at the end of that Apology.
pass_b_english: Dedicating a sacred building to angels or to Saints in heaven is held altogether unlawful.
The ban covers not only offering them sacrifice there, but honoring and invoking them with any rites.
The old custom is not condemned when churches kept the martyrs' memory, thanked God for their victories, and offered the Eucharist to God, which honored holy men greatly.
Rivet's note on the Apology for the Blessed Virgin is the reference.

choices.why: The ancient practice is kept because the offering terminates on God.
